name: Coding Blog
description: Articles on software engineering, system architecture, .NET development, tooling, and practical lessons learned from hands-on experiments.
overview: A technical writing home for documenting practical engineering decisions, experiments, and lessons learned. The published site organizes articles for readers who want implementation detail rather than short announcements.
highlights: Software engineering and system architecture articles
Hands-on .NET and developer-tooling notes
Technical experiments and lessons learned
audience: Engineers looking for practical write-ups and worked examples.

caseStudy.problem: Useful engineering knowledge often gets lost between implementation, experimentation, and the next project.
caseStudy.solution: Publish concrete explanations of architecture, .NET tooling, development practices, and lessons learned.
decisions: Prioritize specific engineering examples over broad announcements.
Keep writing connected to actual experiments and implementation work.
caseStudy.status: The published blog is the source for current articles, topics, and updates.

name: Isolated .NET SDK
description: Install, audit, verify, and remove exact .NET SDK versions in a user-owned directory without changing system-wide SDKs or PATH. Supports PowerShell on Windows and Bash on Linux/macOS.
overview: Use exact .NET SDK versions without modifying the machine-wide installation or PATH. The project focuses on repeatable local SDK management across development and automation environments.
highlights: Install and remove specific SDK versions in a user-owned directory
Audit and verify the installed SDK inventory
PowerShell support on Windows and Bash support on Linux and macOS
audience: Developers and CI maintainers who need predictable SDK versions without system-wide changes.

caseStudy.problem: Different projects can need exact .NET SDK versions without changing the SDK configuration of an entire machine.
caseStudy.solution: Manage selected SDK versions within a user-owned directory, leaving system-wide SDKs and PATH untouched.
decisions: Isolation over global machine changes.
Explicit, verifiable SDK versions.
PowerShell on Windows and Bash on Linux/macOS.
caseStudy.status: Installation, audit, verification, and removal are documented; consult the repository and published docs for current examples and limitations.

name: Copy GitHub Repo
description: PowerShell module for copying or migrating GitHub repositories. Choose a clean Snapshot or history-preserving FullHistory mode, with preview plans and safety checks.
overview: A PowerShell-based approach to copying or migrating GitHub repositories with deliberate choices about source history and a preview of the intended operation.
highlights: Snapshot mode creates a clean copy; FullHistory preserves history
Preview plans before making repository changes
Built-in checks help avoid unsafe copy operations
audience: Repository maintainers migrating projects or creating controlled copies.

caseStudy.problem: Repository copies involve a choice between starting fresh and retaining complete history, with risks around unexpected changes.
caseStudy.solution: Offer deliberate Snapshot and FullHistory modes alongside preview plans and safety checks.
decisions: Make history preservation an explicit choice.
Expose the intended operation before execution.
Prefer safety checks to surprising repository changes.
caseStudy.status: The repository and published documentation describe available commands, requirements, and current behavior.

name: AI Flywheel Specification
description: An evidence-driven AI operating model: execute work, observe outcomes, evaluate evidence, validate improvements, and reuse learning in future execution under defined governance.
overview: Defines the operating rules for a governed improvement cycle in AI-assisted work. Rather than treating each execution as isolated, the specification connects goals, evidence, evaluation, and reusable learning.
highlights: Defines an execution-to-evidence-to-improvement lifecycle
Distinguishes validated learning from unverified observations
Establishes governance and traceability for continued operation
audience: Teams designing evidence-driven, repeatable AI-assisted engineering processes.

caseStudy.problem: AI-assisted work can repeat tasks without accumulating verified learning or clearly governing what happens next.
caseStudy.solution: Define a lifecycle that connects execution, observation, evidence, evaluation, validated improvement, and reuse.
decisions: Treat evidence as distinct from assumption.
Make governance and traceability part of the operating model.
Define the normative rules separately from implementation.
caseStudy.status: The specification repository and its published documentation are authoritative for current requirements and revisions.

name: AI Flywheel Framework
description: Installable, implementation-neutral AI Flywheel framework providing repository onboarding, mission and goal records, lifecycle guidance, evidence capture, and governance.
overview: The installable operating model that brings the AI Flywheel specification into a repository. It provides canonical artifacts and an onboarding process before repository-specific automation is built.
highlights: Installs a canonical .flywheel structure and manifest-driven startup
Provides onboarding, bootstrap missions, and goal records
Captures lifecycle state, evidence, learning, and governance
audience: Repository owners adopting the AI Flywheel operating model.

caseStudy.problem: An operating specification alone does not establish a repeatable, repository-local way to work.
caseStudy.solution: Provide an installable .flywheel structure, manifest-driven startup, bootstrap missions, lifecycle records, and governance guidance.
decisions: Use the manifest as the authoritative entry point.
Remain independent of programming language and toolchain.
Support manual operation before repository-specific tools are built.
caseStudy.status: The framework repository contains the current installation model, operating artifacts, and onboarding guidance.

name: AI Flywheel CLI
description: In-development cross-platform .NET CLI for initializing, managing, validating, and upgrading AI Flywheel installations, missions, and goals.
overview: A planned cross-platform .NET command-line interface for managing Flywheel installations. Its command surface is being developed to make common lifecycle tasks consistent and scriptable.
highlights: Planned installation and initialization commands
Planned mission and goal management, validation, and upgrades
Designed for cross-platform use and machine-readable automation output
audience: Developers planning to operate Flywheel workflows from a terminal or CI pipeline.

caseStudy.problem: Operating the AI Flywheel manually across repositories can make common lifecycle tasks inconsistent.
caseStudy.solution: Develop a cross-platform .NET command-line interface for installation, missions, goals, validation, and upgrades.
decisions: Plan consistent, script-friendly commands.
Keep the command surface cross-platform.
Preserve repository-specific information during planned upgrades.
caseStudy.status: Under active development. Commands and behavior described as planned should not be treated as shipped until verified in the repository.

name: AI Flywheel CLI Python
description: Python 3.11+ CLI for inspecting, validating, installing, and operating AI Flywheel artifacts locally, with safeguards, structured results, and lifecycle commands.
overview: A Python command-line companion for inspecting and operating local AI Flywheel artifacts, with structured results and safeguards around modifications.
highlights: Inspect and validate local Flywheel artifacts
Support installation and lifecycle operations
Use structured command results for automation and diagnostics
audience: Python users and automation authors integrating AI Flywheel operations.

caseStudy.problem: Python workflows need a practical way to inspect and operate local Flywheel artifacts while retaining safeguards.
caseStudy.solution: Provide a Python 3.11+ CLI with inspection, validation, installation, and lifecycle-oriented commands.
decisions: Use structured command results for automation.
Validate artifacts before relying on them.
Keep local operations explicit and safeguarded.
caseStudy.status: Consult the repository for current commands, supported operations, and limitations.

name: AI Flywheel Framework Testing
description: Repeatable framework tests using versioned prompts, fixtures, runners, and captured evidence to assess normal, boundary, failure, and recovery scenarios.
overview: A separate test harness and evidence store for evaluating the AI Flywheel Framework. Test assets and captured outcomes live outside the installable framework to make failures easier to reproduce.
highlights: Versioned prompts, fixtures, and test runners
Normal, boundary, failure, and recovery test scenarios
Durable evidence linked to exact test and framework revisions
audience: Framework contributors and reviewers validating behavior before changes are accepted.

caseStudy.problem: Changes to an AI operating framework need repeatable tests and evidence, not just informal prompts and impressions.
caseStudy.solution: Keep versioned prompts, fixtures, runners, and captured evidence in a separate testing repository.
decisions: Separate test assets from the installable framework.
Tie outcomes to immutable source revisions.
Include boundary, failure, and recovery scenarios.
caseStudy.status: The testing repository records current fixtures, test methods, and published evidence.

name: NuGet Publication Cooldown POC
description: Reproducible PowerShell experiments testing NuGet's .NET 11 RC2 package publication cooldown and its effects on automatic version selection versus explicit restore.
overview: A focused PowerShell proof of concept exploring package publication timing in NuGet and how version selection behaves during a publication cooldown.
highlights: Reproducible experiments for .NET 11 RC2 packages
Compare automatic package version selection against explicit restore
Document observable effects of publication cooldown behavior
audience: .NET package authors and maintainers investigating restore behavior.

caseStudy.problem: Package publication cooldowns can produce confusing differences between implicit version resolution and explicit package restore.
caseStudy.solution: Use reproducible PowerShell experiments to examine .NET 11 RC2 package availability and restore behavior.
decisions: Compare automatic version selection with explicit restore.
Keep the experiment reproducible.
Report observations without overstating general conclusions.
caseStudy.status: This is a proof of concept; see the repository for scripts, observations, and conclusions.
